verdict: Dominion Energy's revenue jumped 24% to $5.6B on surging data-center demand in Virginia, and net income rose to $1.2B, with the company's operating earnings of $1.28 a share just below GAAP EPS of $1.30.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Operating revenues were $5.6B, vs $4.5B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: From continuing operations, vs $1.16 a year ago; attributable net income was $1.2B

kpis.label: Operating EPS (non-GAAP)
kpis.note: Dominion's own headline measure, which strips out market gains and losses and other items it calls non-recurring; vs $1.06 a year ago

kpis.label: High-load revenue
kpis.note: Regulated electric sales to high-load customers — mainly data centers — up 40% from $503M a year ago

segments.name: Regulated electric sales
segments.note: Electricity sold at rates set by regulators, mostly in Virginia and South Carolina — homes ($2,157M), businesses ($1,404M), high-load customers such as data centers ($706M), industry, government and wholesale buyers, plus other regulated charges. Up 25% vs a year ago.

segments.name: Regulated gas sales
segments.note: Natural gas sold at regulated rates to about 500,000 customers in South Carolina, including transportation and storage. Up 8% vs a year ago.

segments.name: Nonregulated and other
segments.note: Power and services sold outside regulated rates — including output from contracted generation such as the Millstone nuclear plant in Connecticut — plus other revenues. Up 19% vs a year ago.

opex.name: Other operations and maintenance
opex.note: Running and maintaining power plants, wires and gas pipes — crews, repairs and day-to-day operations. Up from $850M a year ago as the system grows.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: The cost of plants, grids and equipment wearing out over time.

opex.name: Other taxes
opex.note: Property and other taxes on operations — separate from income tax.

opex.name: Impairment & other
opex.note: Impairment of assets and other charges — writing down the value of assets and related charges — much smaller than the $130M recorded a year ago.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. The direct energy costs are electric fuel and other energy-related purchases ($1,603M), purchased electric capacity ($106M) and purchased gas ($40M). The flow uses net income from continuing operations including noncontrolling interests of $1,275M; net income attributable to Dominion Energy was $1,160M (including a $1M discontinued-operations loss), after $114M attributable to noncontrolling interests. Revenue rows use the 10-Q's revenue disaggregation, grouped, because segment revenue from external customers for Corporate and Other was negative (-$10M); the groups sum exactly to total operating revenue.

takeaways.title: Data centers are driving growth
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 24% to $5,617M. The fastest-growing piece was high-load customers — mainly data centers concentrated in Loudoun County, Virginia — whose regulated electric purchases rose 40% to $706M from $503M. Residential sales rose 26% to $2,157M.

takeaways.title: Virginia is the profit engine
takeaways.text: Dominion Energy Virginia contributed $862M of operating earnings (the company's non-GAAP segment measure), up from $679M a year ago — about three-quarters of the company total. South Carolina added $230M and Contracted Energy $134M, while Corporate and Other lost $87M.

takeaways.title: Near the top of guidance
takeaways.text: Operating earnings were $1.28 a share vs GAAP EPS of $1.30 — the items Dominion strips out were small this quarter. The company said it expects to land in the top half of its 2026 operating EPS guidance of $3.45–$3.69 and reaffirmed its long-term growth, credit and dividend guidance; its release also discusses the proposed merger with NextEra Energy.

oneTimers: The income statement includes $19M of impairment of assets and other charges in Q3, down from $130M a year ago.

GAAP EPS of $1.30 vs operating EPS of $1.28: the items Dominion excludes from operating earnings — mainly gains and losses on its nuclear decommissioning trust funds and mark-to-market moves on economic hedges — netted to only about $0.02 a share this quarter. Over the first nine months those adjustments were much larger, including an $820M charge on nonregulated renewable natural gas facilities, partly offset by trust-fund gains.
otherDetail: Other income of $271M — including $229M of other income (such as gains on nuclear decommissioning trust funds and the allowance for funds used during construction, an amount regulators let the company count as income while projects are being built), $40M of interest income and $2M of equity earnings — less interest and related charges of $623M, for a net $352M cost below operating income.
footerNote: Flow adaptation: Dominion reports no gross-profit line; cost of revenue combines fuel, purchased capacity and purchased gas.
